Explanation: A completed ride is the core value unit: a rider requests transport, an available driver accepts the trip, and the driver takes the rider to the destination.
ANI Technologies operates Ola's ride-hailing platform in India and provides the technology that connects riders and drivers.
Ola has to bring riders and drivers together and make the platform useful enough that drivers are willing to pay for access.
Under the zero-commission approach, Ola can earn from driver access or subscription plans instead of taking a percentage from every fare.
Ola still needs enough riders and drivers in each local market. If either side is missing, the platform becomes less useful.
Ola provides matching and software access. In the subscription model, drivers can pay for access while keeping the fare from rides.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Request — The rider asks Ola to find a suitable nearby driver. | → Provider · Match — Ola sends the trip opportunity to eligible drivers through its software. | ← Provider · Subscription — Drivers can pay Ola for platform access instead of giving Ola a percentage of every ride fare.

Explanation: Ola sets rules for driver eligibility, vehicles, safety, service quality and platform use while following local transport regulation.
Ola reaches riders through its consumer app and drivers through its driver tools and local acquisition programs.
Ola operates the apps, matches requests, supports users, manages safety and maintains the marketplace.
Important resources include rider demand, driver supply, software, trip data, maps, payments integrations and the Ola brand.
People use Ola when they need a cab, auto-rickshaw, bike or other available mobility option.
Riders want a quick way to find transport without searching for a driver themselves.
Ola can give riders several vehicle categories, estimated fares and convenient booking from one app.
Riders can face long waits, cancellations, fare disagreements or limited supply in some places and times.
The rider requests a trip and pays the fare. In Ola's auto bidding model, payment goes directly from rider to driver.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Request — The rider asks Ola to find a suitable nearby driver. | ← Provider · Ride — The driver provides the physical transport from pickup to destination. | → Provider · Fare — In the direct-payment model, the rider pays the fare to the driver.

Explanation: A rider can only book where Ola operates and where a suitable driver is available.
Riders search, book and track available trips in the Ola app.
Riders enter a destination, select an option, take the trip, pay and can provide feedback.
Riders bring trip demand, pickup and destination information, payment and ratings to the marketplace.
Independent drivers provide the physical transport service using cabs, auto-rickshaws, bikes or other eligible vehicles.
Drivers want enough useful trip demand to turn their time and vehicle into income.
Under Ola's zero-commission model, drivers can keep the fare rather than losing a percentage of each ride to platform commission.
Drivers still face fuel, vehicle, maintenance and idle-time costs and need enough trips to make platform access worthwhile.
Drivers accept suitable requests, provide the physical ride and receive the fare from the rider.
Transaction Flows: ← Owner · Match — Ola sends the trip opportunity to eligible drivers through its software. | → Consumer · Ride — The driver provides the physical transport from pickup to destination. | ← Consumer · Fare — In the direct-payment model, the rider pays the fare to the driver. | → Owner · Subscription — Drivers can pay Ola for platform access instead of giving Ola a percentage of every ride fare. | ← Partner · Car / Fleet — Fleet operators make vehicles and managed driver capacity available to the provider side.

Explanation: Drivers and vehicles must meet Ola requirements and applicable licensing, documentation and safety rules.
Drivers use Ola's driver tools to go online, see requests and manage their platform participation.
Drivers go online, accept or bid on eligible requests, complete trips and maintain their vehicle and documents.
Drivers contribute their time, local knowledge, required documents and access to a suitable vehicle.
Fleet operators can register and manage multiple drivers and vehicles through Ola's operator tools.
Fleet operators help put more eligible cars and drivers onto the marketplace.
A fleet benefits when its vehicles and drivers receive enough ride demand to stay productive.
Fleet economics weaken when vehicles sit unused or drivers cannot get enough trips.
Fleet operators add and manage vehicles and drivers that can provide rides through Ola.
Transaction Flows: → Provider · Car / Fleet — Fleet operators make vehicles and managed driver capacity available to the provider side.

Explanation: Vehicles, drivers and operators must meet Ola and local documentation and quality requirements.
Ola provides an operator portal with tools for drivers, vehicles, performance, banking and quality checks.
Fleet operators onboard drivers and vehicles and manage availability, quality and performance.
Fleet operators contribute vehicles, driver relationships and local operating capacity.
